title: CLO 2025.1 - Denim Wash Effect Preset
description: CLO 2025.1 new version fully upgraded to further enhance your work efficiency! The new version adds preset denim wash effects, allowing easy application of various denim washing techniques (such as stone wash, enzyme wash, and bleaching).
transcript:
This video introduces the water-washing effect preset function of the bullfrog fabric.  
It can achieve the appearance of a real bullfrog fabric.  
Starting from version 2025.1, the material type "Diningbo" has been added.  
Using this function, you can adjust the water-washing process presets and various parameters to display different water-washing effects.  
This function is based on the bullfrog texture and the basic texture map for water-washing.  
We will use this bullfrog fabric to demonstrate the function.  

First, select the bullfrog fabric in the object window.  
Then, in the property editor below, change the material type to Diningbo.  
When the material type is set to Diningbo, you will see the water-washing process type option appear below.  
Use the water-washing type to select the bullfrog fabric.  
Select the water-washing process to preview the effect.  
According to the selected water-washing type, the detailed properties or parameters below will change accordingly.  
You can freely adjust these parameters.  

Next, we will quickly understand the different water-washing types that can be displayed through this image.  

First, the default setting corresponds to the water-washing type.  
It refers to the original bullfrog fabric that has not been water-washed.  
Only the original fabric’s texture map is applied.  

The Diningbo type is the most basic water-washing process.  
It can evenly color and soften the fabric.  
At the same time, it retains the original color of the bullfrog fabric to the greatest extent.  

The speed-washing type can be applied through the light pattern.  
It slightly fades the color and softens the fabric.  
The effect resembles fabric worn many times, while avoiding obvious discoloration.  

The nature-painting effect adds floating friction to the fabric during washing.  
It has a natural painting effect and forms a clear contrast pattern.  

The Dining-washing type is used for special chemical processing.  
It forms a strong contrast compared to the other Dining-washing types.  
The visual effect is distinct.  

The Dining-washing technique makes the color of the bullfrog fabric lighter.  
The strength of the processing can range from subtle tones to an almost white multi-layer effect.  

The Dining-washing technique can achieve a natural anti-painting effect with even discoloration.  
It makes the bullfrog fabric appear in a subtle and unified light tone.  

Finally, the customized Dining-washing type supports applying custom Dining-washing patterns.  
It allows infinite expansion of the individuality of Dining-washing effects.  
It achieves a unique design expression.  

Now let's return to the Dining-washing interface.  
We will apply two Dining-washing types, Dining-washing and Dining-washing, to this bullfrog fabric.  
Then, we will see how to adjust their parameters to display different bullfrog Dining-washing effects.  

First, in the property editor,  
change the Dining-washing process type to Dining-washing.  
You can see the Dining-washing effect on the entire pants in the 3D window.  
Click the small triangle.  
The Dining-washing pattern corresponding to the Dining-washing type will appear below.  
The basic pattern and the fabric naturally integrate,  
thus showing the bullfrog Dining-washing effect of the Dining-washing type.  

If you do not use Dining-washing, you can also add the Dining-washing pattern you want.  
Then the Dining-washing process type will automatically switch to user customized.  
This way, you can achieve the customized Dining-washing effect you desire.  

Next, we will look at the detailed properties of the selected Dining-washing type.  

The first property is discoloration intensity.  
As the name suggests, this controls the overall intensity of the discoloration effect.  
Moving the slider to the right increases the value.  
The contrast in the dark areas of the pants will become more pronounced.  
The maximum value creates the feeling of long-term wear.  

Next is the mixing mode below.  
Click the drop-down menu to switch between various mixing options,  
such as normal, flat bottom, and green.  
These options determine how the Dining-washing effect mixes with the bullfrog fabric pattern.  

Specifically, the Dining-washing function naturally increases contrast.  
It darkens the dark parts of the Dining-washing pattern and brightens the bright parts of the original pattern.  
Due to the highly realistic simulation of the Dining-washing function,  
the discoloration effects closely resemble those in the actual Dining-washing process.  

Therefore, it is recommended that in most Dining-washing settings,  
you use the Dining-washing function for the most natural and realistic results.  

The absorption of the bottom parameter determines the depth and width of the Dining-washing effect absorbed by the fabric.  
Increasing this value enlarges the range of Dining-washing effects,  
creating a more natural and harmonious look.  

The duration of the week controls the length of the Dining-washing time.  
Increasing this value extends the washing time,  
removing more dye from the jeans.  
This allows the overall color of the pants to become lighter.  

Increase the value for subtle effects.  
We are demonstrating the last Dining-washing effect.  
However, to apply this option,  
you must pre-apply sewing wrinkles in the corresponding area.  

Now, as we increase the Dining-washing value,  
you can see it applied to the sides of the pants.  
The texture of the sewing wrinkles becomes darker and the contours clearer.  
Conversely, lowering the value makes the wrinkles more blurred.  

By pre-applying sewing wrinkles and adjusting the crease number,  
you can create a more realistic cowhide creasing water-wash effect.  

Next, change the water-washing technique to rinsing.  
After changing the water-washing type, you will see the overall color of the pants become brighter,  
as if rinsed with a chemical.  
You will also notice the detailed options below differ from the previous 10 model types.  

First is rinsing concentration, which sets the intensity of the water-washing effect.  
Increasing this value enhances the water-washing effect, maximizing the rinsing effect,  
removing more color from the cowhide fabric to make it brighter.  
Reducing this value shows a lighter rinsing effect.  

For rinsing, we can change the mixing mode.  
The rinsing mode is called soft light.  
The contrast of soft light is less strong,  
so the rinsed areas smoothly blend with the original cowhide fabric.  

Therefore, depending on the mixing option chosen,  
even using the same water-washing type, you can achieve various water-washing effects.  

Finally, you can adjust other parameters, such as absorbency or crease wear, to enhance detail performance.  
Especially on the rinsed pants,  
the water-washing effect can be added to creased areas,  
showing a more three-dimensional discoloration effect.  
This creates realistic wear and tear marks, not just simple color fading,  
thus presenting a more layered craftsmanship effect.  

When choosing a different water-washing type, the adjustment parameters below will also differ,  
but the adjustment logic remains the same.  

Using the water-washing preset, you can select the water-washing type you need in the attribute editor,  
and adjust the detailed attributes.  
This will quickly present your cowhide fabric in a more realistic manner.

chunks.content: ## Introduction to Water-Washing Effect Preset in CLO 2025.1 This section explains the new water-washing effect preset function introduced in CLO 2025.1, focusing on the "Diningbo" material type and its application to bullfrog fabric. Key terms include water-washing process presets, bullfrog texture, and Diningbo material type. The water-washing effect preset simulates realistic denim wash effects on bullfrog fabric by using the newly added material type "Diningbo" in CLO version 2025.1. This function leverages the bullfrog texture along with a basic texture map to replicate various water-washing styles. Users can select bullfrog fabric in the object window, change its material type to Diningbo in the property editor, and then choose from different water-washing process types to preview and adjust effects with customizable parameters. --- ## Overview of Water-Washing Types for Bullfrog Fabric This section details the different water-washing types available, describing their visual effects and technical characteristics. Important terms include Diningbo type, speed-washing, nature-painting effect, Dining-washing, and customized Dining-washing. - **Default:** Represents the original bullfrog fabric without any water-washing effect applied; only the original texture map is used. - **Diningbo Type:** Basic water-washing effect that evenly colors and softens fabric while retaining most of the original fabric color. - **Speed-Washing Type:** Uses light patterns to slightly fade and soften the fabric, mimicking wear without obvious discoloration. - **Nature-Painting Effect:** Adds floating friction during washing, creating natural paint-like contrast patterns. - **Dining-Washing Type:** Mimics special chemical processing, producing strong contrast and lighter fabric colors ranging from subtle tones to nearly white multilayer effects. It also achieves natural, even discoloration with a subtle, unified light tone. - **Customized Dining-Washing:** Allows users to apply custom patterns, enabling infinite variations and unique design expressions. --- ## Applying and Adjusting Dining-Washing Types This section covers how to apply Dining-washing presets and adjust parameters to create diverse bullfrog fabric effects. Technical terms include property editor, discoloration intensity, mixing mode, and sewing wrinkles. To apply Dining-washing effects: 1. Set the material type to Diningbo and choose the desired Dining-washing process type. 2. The corresponding Dining-washing pattern appears below the property editor, integrating naturally with the fabric. 3. Alternatively, adding a custom Dining-washing pattern automatically switches the process type to user customized, allowing bespoke effects. Key adjustable properties include: - **Discoloration Intensity:** Controls the overall strength of the discoloration effect; higher values increase contrast, simulating long-term wear. - **Mixing Mode:** Options such as normal, flat bottom, and green determine how the Dining-washing effect blends with the bullfrog fabric pattern. The function enhances realism by darkening dark areas and brightening bright areas in the pattern. - **Absorption of the Bottom Parameter:** Defines the depth and spread of the washing effect on the fabric; increasing it creates a more natural and harmonious look. - **Duration of the Week:** Controls the washing time length; longer durations remove more dye, lightening the fabric color. - **Sewing Wrinkles:** Pre-applying sewing wrinkles and adjusting crease numbers enhances realism by simulating water-wash effects on creased fabric areas; increasing Dining-washing values makes wrinkles darker and contours clearer.

chunks.content: - **Absorption of the Bottom Parameter:** Defines the depth and spread of the washing effect on the fabric; increasing it creates a more natural and harmonious look. - **Duration of the Week:** Controls the washing time length; longer durations remove more dye, lightening the fabric color. - **Sewing Wrinkles:** Pre-applying sewing wrinkles and adjusting crease numbers enhances realism by simulating water-wash effects on creased fabric areas; increasing Dining-washing values makes wrinkles darker and contours clearer. --- ## Using Rinsing Water-Washing Type and Parameter Adjustments This section explains the rinsing water-washing type and how to customize its parameters for realistic fabric effects. Key terms include rinsing concentration, soft light mixing mode, absorbency, and crease wear. Switching to the rinsing water-washing type brightens the fabric color, simulating chemical rinsing. Parameters include: - **Rinsing Concentration:** Adjusts the intensity of the rinsing effect; higher values produce stronger washing, removing more color. - **Mixing Mode (Soft Light):** Provides a smoother, less contrasted blend between rinsed areas and original fabric for natural transitions. - **Absorbency and Crease Wear:** These parameters add detail by enhancing the washing effect in creased areas, creating three-dimensional discoloration and realistic wear marks instead of simple fading. Different water-washing types have distinct parameters, but the logic of adjusting intensity, blending, and detail remains consistent. --- ## Summary of Water-Washing Preset Usage This section summarizes how to efficiently use the water-washing preset to achieve realistic denim effects on bullfrog fabric. Users select the desired water-washing type from the attribute editor and fine-tune detailed parameters to quickly produce authentic-looking cowhide fabric effects. The presets simulate various real-world washing processes, offering a range of visual styles from subtle discoloration to strong chemical treatments, with customizable patterns and realistic crease wear. This enables designers to create highly detailed and individualized denim wash appearances in CLO 2025.1.
